newsitem.title: USA: NIAGARA MOHAWK SETS HYDRO CONTRACT CHANGES.
newsitem.headline: NIAGARA MOHAWK SETS HYDRO CONTRACT CHANGES.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp said it has agreed to restructure its power purchase contract with Glen Park Associates, the owner of a 33 megawatt hydro plant in Jefferson County, N.Y.

Glen Park said it, in turn will now seek to restructure its debt held by Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association-College Retirement Equities Fund. Known as TIAA-CREF, the fund the largest pension fund in the U.S.
The restructured agreement will reduce power purchase costs $24 million over the next 10 years, Niagara Mohawk said with providing further details.

Spokeswoman Kerry Burns said no cash payments are ivolved in the restructuring, adding the resulting agreement with be filed with the New York Public Service Commission "under trade secrets protection."

The compnay said the hydro plant was among 15 hydro projects that were originally included in its March agreement in principle with 19 independent power producers to terminate or restructure 44 purchase contracts representing 90 percent of the utility's above-market power costs.
Niagara Mohawk noted its offer to the 15 hydro plants was withdrawn when a settlement could not be reached.
The three developers who own the plants agreed to pursue settlements with Niagara Mohawk on an individual basis.

This withdrawal, it said last month, reduced the portion of above-market costs covered by the agreement to 80 percent while leaving the proposed payment the same -- $3.6 million in cash and 44 million common shares, respresenting 25 percent of the company's common.
The Glen Park project, operated by Mercer Cos, a general partner of Glen Park Associates, represents about 25 percent of the above-market costs attributed to the 15 projects.

F. Michael Tucker, a Mercer partner, said "This agreement will give us some certainty in the competitive electricity marketplace. We are hopeful that we will be able to restructure our debt and reduce operating expenses so we will be able to continue to meet our financial obligations and provide immediate and significant rate discounts."
The Glen Park Hydro agreement is subject to a number of contingencies that require third party approvals, Niagara Mohawk said in a statement.
It said the agreement is expected to be finalized by year end. In the meantime, the utility will continue contract restructuring discussions on its remaining hydro projects.
